expressions.cue: A person visits again after a gap of one year. Write only the gap expression using 年ぶり and kanji or Arabic numerals, not the duration of the visit.
expressions.explanation: 一年ぶり marks a year since the previous occurrence. The visit itself need not last a year. This is a supplied-meaning expression drill, not an independent test of the Grammar construction.

expressions.cue: A club holds an event again after a six-month gap. Write only the gap expression with the month-duration unit followed by ぶり. Use kanji or Arabic numerals; か月, ヶ月, 箇月, カ月, ヵ月 and ケ月 are allowed.
expressions.explanation: 六か月ぶり is ろっかげつぶり. It describes the gap before the repeated event, not six months spent holding it or a fixed count of days. The month spellings do not change the reading.
